title: Merge Settings
prompt: A preferences screen has default settings and user overrides. Write a function that returns a new object where user settings replace matching default keys while untouched defaults remain.

explanation.beginner:
Example: mergeSettings({"theme":"light","density":"comfortable"}, {"theme":"dark"}) produces {"theme":"dark","density":"comfortable"}. The result must follow this precise rule: A preferences screen has default settings and user overrides. Write a function that returns a new object where user settings replace matching default keys while untouched defaults remain. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “adds new override keys”: input [{"theme":"light"},{"beta":true}] produces {"theme":"light","beta":true}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.

Tempting mistake: Do not hard-code the first example: the adds new override keys case changes the input contract’s boundary or shape. Compare the actual outputs rather than only checking whether both are truthy.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “adds new override keys”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
